text:
ashwin: FYI noticed a tenant-triggered spiral in eu-west last night where their background batch + a scheduled preload flooded egress and pushed traffic into shared pools. Dedicated slices saturated and we saw 4x tail latency for smaller tenants.

olga: which tenant? any ID / traces?

ashwin: tenant id T-8342. alert from SLO monitor at 23:07 UTC. quick grep of egress series: 
```
# egress bytes/s per slice
23:00  slice-eu-west-1: 120MB/s
23:05  slice-eu-west-1: 480MB/s <-- spike
23:10  shared-pool-eu-west: 300MB/s
23:15  error-rate small-tenants: 1.8% -> 4.6%
```

sre-bot: [ALERT] large-egress-spike T-8342 -> triggered routing-fallback (auto).

devin: Did the auto fallback route correctly to a lower-cost model or did it just push to shared capacity?

ashwin: It pushed to shared capacity. Fallback policy was 'compatible-variant' only, no egress-cap limiting. That let egress growth cascade.

samir: Oof. Two things: 1) per-tenant egress soft-quotas (burst window) and 2) per-AZ slice throttling so a noisy tenant in one AZ doesn't cause remote slices to reassign.

olga: +1. Proposal: add an az-scoped throttle policy and a per-tenant egress token bucket that gates fallback routing. If token bucket exhausted, fallback goes to degraded model or rejects (depending on tier).

devin: rough config mockup i tested locally:
```
policies:
  egress_burst:
    type: token_bucket
    capacity: 100MB
    refill_rate: 10MB/s
    scope: tenant
  az_slice_throttle:
    type: max_inflight_by_az
    max_inflight: 80
    scope: az
    action: slow-path
```
If az_slice_throttle triggers, route new allocs to cold-pool where we have stricter egress policing.

katie: For Dedicated customers we should make this opt-in with clear UX; they may prefer reserved latency over an automatic throttle. Also flagging the cost impact: moving to cold-pool increases CPU+net bills.

samir: Good point. For Dedicated slices, policy should be 'canary throttle' where we throttle 5% of new requests first and measure. No global change without approval.

ashwin: Runbook additions — quick kill commands we used during the incident:
```
# admin-cli route toggle
admin-cli route set-policy --tenant T-8342 --policy egress-bucket=low
# migrate allocs off slice
admin-cli alloc drain --slice slice-eu-west-1 --scope tenants_except T-8342
```

olga: Can we add a short-circuit at the proxy layer to rate-limit egress per-tenant before the fallback decision? That prevents the fallback from ever seeing the large burst.

devin: yes, we can add an L7 token bucket plugin in the shared proxy. Low-risk change: enforce only on non-Dedicated by default. I'll draft the PR.

katie: timeline? if we want this for next month we need a canary in eu-west and a short doc for sales + support.

devin: I'll open the PR today with tests for token bucket and a simple canary toggle. tagging @ashwin for metrics dashboard queries and @olga for runbook edits.

ashwin: thanks — I'll add the metric panels and a playbook entry. Also scheduling a quick sync tomorrow 09:30 UTC to align on canary thresholds.

olga: adding to eng-infra calendar. :thumbsup:

sre-bot: [NOTE] incident T-8342 closed at 23:52 UTC. root cause: tenant background preload + fallback policy gap.

devin: follow-up action items: PR # (will link), eu-west canary (5% traffic), runbook patch, support notice draft.

samir: and cost review after canary; we need to quantify cold-pool penalty so PM can weigh SLA tradeoffs.

ashwin: agreed. good first step.
